newsitem.title: GERMANY: German SPD rules out deal for major tax reform.
newsitem.headline: German SPD rules out deal for major tax reform.

text.p: German opposition Social Democrats (SPD) have ruled out reaching an agreement with the government on a major tax reform plan, the party's parliamentary chief said on Tuesday.
"It was clear that there will be no agreement on the tax laws for 1998 and 1999," Peter Struck told reporters.
German SPD rules out deal for major tax reform
But he said it was still possible to agree to elimination of a corporate asset tax and reductions in non-wage labour costs, Struck said.

Members of the coalition and opposition parties were expected to continue negotiations on Wednesday. The coalition passed a tax package in the lower house of parliament, but it was blocked by the SPD majority in the upper house, forcing the two sides to negotiate in a mediation committee.
